scope: Step-by-step surgical update report for SARA Lite OS, Lite pillars, VNCE WFH readiness, and C# Office Suite impact based on work completed today since after 2am.

completed_today_since_2am: Updated mythosreport.json with a live AMIP/AMIPI audit result
Previously established protocol expansion inputs remain available: amip_amipi_surgical_expansion_plan.json, vnce_remote_node_requirements.json, and protocol_expansion_unified_patch.json

core_lite.readiness_for_wfh: not yet online as a distinct OS module
what_is_already_present: AMIP envelope and workflow_state concepts already exist in the current CORE runtime design.
Machine profile and deterministic shaping are already described in the Lite plans.

implementation_steps.step: Extract a small CORE-Lite wrapper that exposes envelope building, workflow_state, machine_profile resolution, and deterministic defaults for SARA Lite OS startup.
Bind CORE-Lite output to the planned AMIP/AMIPI schema store under the OS runtime layout.

notes: CORE-Lite is one of the easier bounded extractions because the underlying concepts already exist.
It must remain non-routing and deterministic.

control_lite.readiness_for_wfh: partial but not yet packaged as an OS service
what_is_already_present: CONTROL-side AMIP normalization exists conceptually in current plans and Gen1 control code.
VNCE lifecycle and AMIPI routing behavior already have identified runtime surfaces.

implementation_steps.step: Create a CONTROL-Lite service wrapper that exposes AMIP normalization, route_bucey_shunt behavior, and explicit route_class handling for VNCE and self.evolve.
Wire byte-level shunt decode enforcement into the OS-facing control path rather than leaving it only at planning level.
Add and verify routing_intent='self.evolve' and keep dry_run-first behavior enforced.

notes: CONTROL-Lite is the core gating path for WFH readiness.
If this stays only at design level, VNCE-based WFH sessions remain blocked.

security_lite.readiness_for_wfh: not yet sufficiently online for trusted LAN/internet WFH
what_is_already_present: SECURITY-first validation, STABLES concepts, and VNCE attestation are already represented in the current security plan and audit findings.
Trust-policy and audit-log paths are already defined for SARA Lite OS.

implementation_steps.step: Bind SECURITY-Lite to a real trust-policy file for local_only, lan, and internet posture decisions.
Implement signature validation for NBS delta bundles and tie it into self_evolve and update-sync gates.
Harden LAN-first trust checks and quarantine behavior for VNCE resume and reconnect cases.

notes: SECURITY-Lite is the main blocker for moving from local-safe to WFH-trusted behavior.
Internet-strict behavior should remain disabled until LAN staging passes.

mama_lite.readiness_for_wfh: summary logic planned but cockpit-facing implementation still needed
what_is_already_present: Low-strain, ADA-first, and voice-first defaults are already defined in the OS plans.
MAMA-Lite is already designated to summarize AMIP/AMIPI and self_evolve results.

implementation_steps.step: Create a minimal MAMA-Lite summary adapter that renders session, trust, and evolution status in human-readable text.
Wire MAMA-Lite into the cockpit UI and the VNCE return summary surface.

notes: This is important for ADA and WFH usability but is not the first technical blocker.

what_is_already_present: SDK-Lite is already defined as adapter-only with AMIPI and VNCE packaging responsibilities.
The self_evolve AI profile and protocol spec are already documented for SDK-Lite request-building.

implementation_steps.step: Implement the request builder surfaces for VNCE and self_evolve without adding direct execution or networking bypasses.
Add remote endpoint metadata handling for server_host, server_port, transport_security, and reconnect policy under CONTROL governance.

notes: SDK-Lite is still the least online of the five Lite pillars.
It must remain a packaging surface and never a direct router.

what_is_already_present: Snapshot, map, schema, delta, and rebuild rules are already fully planned.
Self_evolve and update-sync governance has now been specified.

implementation_steps.step: Create the NBS-Lite service and filesystem roots for snapshots, maps, schemas, deltas, and rebuild state.
Implement dry-run reconstruction and last-known-good rollback as the default update behavior.

notes: NBS-Lite is critical for safe evolution and continuity but currently remains a design layer, not a boot-ready implementation.
Without it, self-repair and self_evolve remain conceptual only.

sara_lite_cockpit.readiness_for_wfh: not yet available as the operator-facing UI
what_is_already_present: The cockpit structure, allowed actions, blocked actions, and ADA profile are already specified.
Desktop entry and service names are already identified.

implementation_steps.step: Build a minimal single-window cockpit executable with health, trust, continuity, and tool-availability panels.
Add the safe-mode banner, guided prompts, and quick-launch hooks for Geany/VSCodium after successful boot policy load.

notes: The cockpit is a usability multiplier for WFH but still needs actual implementation work.
It must remain request-based and never directly override routing or security.

what_is_done: Base SARA Lite OS identity and desktop form have been fully specified.
IDE and devtools integration has been defined for VSCodium, Geany, Python/C#/shell tooling, and systemd integration.
Micro-SARA pillar placement, NBS-Lite continuity rules, and cockpit requirements have been mapped.
Self-evolve governance and AI Profile extensions have been defined as additive protocol specs.
Mythos-style boundary auditing has been recorded with a current PARTIAL_PASS status.
what_remains: Actually assemble the Linux image and rootfs according to the spec.
Create the systemd service graph and file layout under /opt/sara-vnce and /var/lib/sara-lite.
Implement the Lite pillar wrappers and bootstrap scripts.
Run boot and WFH session validation on target x86_64 hardware.
Prove LAN-first trust, VNCE session start/resume, and local IDE behavior end-to-end.
dependencies_on_sara_lite_os: XFCE or MATE with ADA defaults
notes: The OS build is now well specified, but it remains primarily a blueprint until the image is actually assembled and boot-tested.
The biggest remaining gap is runtime wiring, not more planning.

csharp_office_suite_impact.overall_assessment: A separate C# codebase is probably not required, but the current visible Office Suite build is not yet proven to act as the VNCE server for SARA Lite OS as-is.

reason: The current workspace planning explicitly noted that the VNCE listener/acceptor boundary was not confirmed in the visible C# search results.
SARA Lite OS expects a server boundary with AMIP intake normalization, shunt header emission, session registry, and audit bridging.

minimal_csharp_changes_or_new_build_targ.item: Add a bounded VNCE listener or acceptor boundary for remote SARA Lite OS nodes.
Add an AMIP intake normalizer and a Bucey shunt-header emitter so incoming VNCE requests are converted into CONTROL-governed envelopes.
Add session registry, correlation tracking, and audit logging for session start, resume, disconnect, and close.
likely_modules: local config or JSON profile files

build_and_deployment_recommendation.shared_office_suite_build_with_config_on: possible only if the shared binary gains the bounded VNCE server surfaces and they are enabled through config/profile rather than a fully separate branch

csharp_office_suite_impact.recommended_path: Prefer one shared Office Suite codebase with a SARA Lite OS deployment profile and feature-gated VNCE server mode, rather than a fully separate product build, unless security packaging or customer deployment isolation forces a dedicated build target.
notes: The missing piece is not necessarily a new product, but a clearly bounded server-side integration surface.

If the current Office Suite binary already contains hidden server hooks not visible in the searched workspace, then config-only enablement may be enough; otherwise a small bounded implementation pass is needed.

reason: CONTROL and SECURITY behavior is planned and partially mirrored from current Gen1 concepts, but the Lite runtime and confirmed C# VNCE server boundary are not yet online.
LAN-first trust and resume handling are not yet proven end-to-end in the SARA Lite OS form.
The micro-SARA pillar layout and AMIP/AMIPI/shunt rules are strongly specified.
The actual boot-time Lite modules and NBS-backed runtime are still waiting to be wired into the OS image.
The IDE/devtool layer is the most concrete portion of the SARA Lite OS spec and can likely come online once the image is built.
It still depends on actual packaging into the ISO and successful desktop boot validation.

wfh_readiness.short_summary: SARA Lite OS is architecturally well defined for WFH, local reasoning, and node-side development, but the current state is still pre-online: the blueprint is mature, the runtime wiring is not yet complete.

blocking_items: No confirmed C# VNCE server boundary in the visible Office Suite code for SARA Lite OS to connect to.
CONTROL-Lite, SECURITY-Lite, and SDK-Lite are not yet extracted or packaged as real OS services/modules.
NBS-Lite runtime, snapshot engine, and rollback/rebuild services are still planned rather than implemented.
The cockpit UI is specified but not yet built.
The Linux image has not yet been assembled and boot-tested on target WFH hardware.
LAN-first trust and STABLES resume behavior have not yet been validated end-to-end in the new OS form.

recommended_next_steps.step: Implement and package CONTROL-Lite plus SECURITY-Lite as the first real SARA Lite OS services.
recommended_next_steps.why: These two layers are the gating path for safe WFH VNCE sessions.

recommended_next_steps.step: Add the bounded C# VNCE server boundary and create a SARA Lite OS deployment profile for the Office Suite.
recommended_next_steps.why: Without a server boundary, the remote node cannot complete real WFH sessions.

recommended_next_steps.step: Bring SDK-Lite online as a request-builder and remote-endpoint packaging layer only.
recommended_next_steps.why: This unlocks AMIPI, VNCE packaging, and self_evolve request flow without violating routing rules.

recommended_next_steps.step: Implement NBS-Lite snapshot, dry-run rebuild, and rollback services using the already-defined filesystem layout.
recommended_next_steps.why: This is required for continuity, safe updates, and the self_evolve protocol.

recommended_next_steps.step: Build the cockpit UI and wire MAMA-Lite summaries into it.
recommended_next_steps.why: This is the main operator-facing usability layer for WFH and ADA-first use.

recommended_next_steps.step: Assemble the actual SARA Lite OS image and run LAN-first smoke tests: boot, attestation, VNCE connect, local reasoning, and local IDE launch.
recommended_next_steps.why: This converts the current plan set into a verified WFH-capable platform.
